## Learning goals

- I can tell where I am in the file system.
- I can create, copy, move, and read files in my own practice folder.
- I can use built-in help before running an unfamiliar command.

## Before you start

Open **Terminal** on your Linux computer. Work inside your own home folder. Don't paste commands from a website unless you understand them and your teacher has approved them.

## Try the essential commands

| Task | Command | What you should see |
|---|---|---|
| Show your location | `pwd` | A full path ending with your user or current folder |
| List files | `ls -la` | Names, hidden files, and permissions |
| Make a practice folder | `mkdir -p ~/tej-practice` | A new folder in your home directory |
| Enter the folder | `cd ~/tej-practice` | Your prompt moves to the practice folder |
| Make a text file | `nano notes.txt` | A simple text editor |
| Read the file | `cat notes.txt` | The text appears in the terminal |
| Copy the file | `cp notes.txt notes-backup.txt` | Two files appear when you run `ls` |
| Move or rename it | `mv notes-backup.txt commands.txt` | The backup has its new name |
| Read help | `man ls` or `ls --help` | The command's documentation |
| Inspect processes | `top` or `htop` | Live CPU and memory activity |

`~` means your home folder. `.` means the current folder. `/` is the top of the whole file system.

## Activity

Create `~/tej-practice`. Add a text file that records three commands and what each one does. Copy the file, rename the copy, and show both files to a partner.

## Check your work

Run `pwd` and `ls -la`. You should be inside `tej-practice` and see both text files. Save a screenshot or short command log for your class work.
